title: Everything Meta Ad creators throw at you... the pixel, lookalikes, ob...
description: Everything Meta Ad creators throw at you... the pixel, lookalikes, objectives, placements, explained simply. Save this.
transcript: Meta flew me out to Silicon Valley and I've just been in the room with over a thousand advertisers that spend tens of billions on meta ads every year. I've heard lots of jargon, so today I'm going to break it down for you and explain what it actually means. Reach is simply how many people were your ads put in front of. Impressions is how many times your ads were seen. Different from reach because the same person might see your ads multiple times. Conversion rate typically refers to percentage of people that converted after they clicked on one of your ads. Lookalike Audience, which is a group of people that are very similar to another group of people. You upload a customer list into Meta and say, create me a lookalike audience. Meta will then analyze the data points and then they will create an audience people that are similar to them that you may want to target. MetaPixel, which is code that you put on your website that allows you to track the actions that people take after they click on your ad so you can see what pages they looked at, whether they purchased or became a lead. That information is then fed back into your MetaAd account which allows your ad campaigns to optimize properly and get you more of the actions that you want to get. UGC, which is user generated content, it's where people are explaining their experience with a product or service, making recommendations, demonstrating the features. My favorite version of UGC is to work with creators and influencers. Their scroll stopping power really helps improve performance and then their recommendation carries weight, so conversion rates are higher too.
